rationale: Food science review on chocolate processing and fortification. The oil and Parkinson terms do not identify a cold-pressed peanut oil resting tremor study.
Experimental iron injury and a nitric-oxide synthase inhibitor were the subject of the study. The neurologic setting and oil mention do not establish a dietary peanut oil contrast or resting tremor.
Review of culinary spices in neurologic disorders. It is a citation lead and provides no independent cooked curry leaf freezing-events comparison.
The original fly toxin experiment tested orally exposed curry leaf extract and reported climbing and jumping. Neither function measures freezing episodes in people.
Isolongifolene is an isolated compound in a rotenone rat study with motor task results. The experiment does not compare cooked curry leaf or count clinical freezing episodes.
Glut1 deficiency crossover compared safflower oil with triheptanoin. The disabling paroxysmal-event count differs from clinical Parkinson bradykinesia and oil pressing grade was unreported.
Topical black cumin oil with manual procedures in knee osteoarthritis had reported fatigue results. The route and associated procedures leave a whole ground-seed effect unresolved.
Review of traditional interventions for mild or moderate acute COVID. Use as citation follow-through and resolve overlap with randomized seed or oil trials before interpretation.
Ground seed capsules were compared with psyllium for premenstrual symptoms. The physical domain was inconclusive and individual fatigue estimates were unreported.
Investigational NP-101 combined with cancer immunotherapy, with exposure and adverse-event context. No comparison of ground seed on Parkinson fatigue severity.
Open-label Egyptian COVID trial. Day-four fatigue was recorded in 12/30 assigned Nigella oil and 25/30 standard-care controls. Product is seed oil and fatigue presence is an acute symptom.
Review of herbal treatment in hypothyroidism. It may cite prior Nigella trials but adds no independent Parkinson or ground-seed fatigue estimate.
A multi-ingredient food bar changed a sprint-derived fatigue index in cadets. This index measures decline in sprint power and cannot isolate nigella or clinical fatigue.
Oral seed extract lengthened time to exhaustion in an animal swimming test. This is a physical performance measure rather than Parkinson fatigue severity.
Treadmill-exercised rats received hydroethanolic extract. Splenocyte response relates to exercise and immunity, with no clinical fatigue result.
Herbal preparation patent. The indexed formulation record provides no independently controlled oral ground-seed Parkinson fatigue outcome.
Patent describes a seed-containing herbal composition. It supplies no verified clinical Parkinson fatigue severity result or independent cohort.
Mechanistic review on coconut oil in relation to Parkinson disease. A review hypothesis supplies no primary randomized refined coconut oil fall-count result.
The subject is industrial dust control and material falling in an ore bin, with no human or animal fall outcome.
Study identifies the cause of bacterial canker in kiwifruit plants. It has no consumed fruit or neurologic gait outcome.
External traditional preparation in a pediatric GI context. The patent gives no evaluated oral ground nutmeg or Parkinson constipation comparison.
Donkey-hide gelatin paste patent with mixed ingredient use. No boiled lentils-only intervention or verified insomnia outcome in people with Parkinson disease.
Celery and other plant extracts were used to study insect host choice. They were not test foods in a clinical swallowing study.
